factors.label: Days since the last development event
factors.description: Days between the date of assessment and the most recent public development event in the source repository. The abandonment definition rests on this quantity, so it is the factor with the largest influence on the score.

factors.label: Active contributors
factors.description: Distinct accounts that produced at least one event in the trailing 90 days. A package with several active contributors survives the departure of one of them.

factors.label: Days since the last release
factors.description: Days since the most recent version was published to the registry. A long gap beside continuing commits means a maintained but unreleased package, which is a different condition from abandonment.

factors.label: Change in downloads
factors.description: Downloads in the last 90 days against the 90 days before that. A falling series means the consumers are leaving, which is the consumption side of the same question.

factors.label: Active contributors
factors.description: Distinct accounts that produced at least one event in the trailing 90 days. A package with several active contributors survives the departure of one of them.

factors.label: Days since the last development event
factors.description: Days between the date of assessment and the most recent public development event in the source repository. The abandonment definition rests on this quantity, so it is the factor with the largest influence on the score.

factors.label: Concentration of effort
factors.description: Share of events in the window produced by the single most active account. A share near one means the package depends on one person, which is the condition the published score is meant to surface.

factors.label: Age of the package
factors.description: Days since the first version was published. A young package has a higher rate of abandonment than an established one, independently of its current activity.

unresolved.label: Not published on the registry
unresolved.remedy: The entry is a path or git dependency, which carries no registry history, so no adoption forecast or maintenance score can be derived for it
